figures.finding: The United States Minor Outlying Islands have no law of their own; the federal Fair Labor Standards Act's child-labour section (212) reaches only those of them it names (Wake Island and Johnston Island), where 'oppressive child labor' (employing anyone under sixteen, save a parent's own child outside manufacturing, mining and hazardous work, or anyone sixteen or seventeen in work declared hazardous) is barred; on Midway, Palmyra, Kingman Reef, Baker, Howland, Jarvis and Navassa the Act's wage, hours and child-labour sections don't apply, and no other minimum age was found.

value.follows: United States federal law (FLSA 29 U.S.C. 203(l), 212, 213(f)) where it names the island

figures.applies: Wake Island and Johnston Island only (FLSA s. 213(f)); the other islands: not reached by the Act.

sources.said: (f) Employment in foreign countries and certain United States territories The provisions of sections 206 , 207 , 211 , and 212 of this title shall not apply with respect to any employee whose services during the workweek are performed in a workplace within a foreign country or within territory under the jurisdiction of the United States other than the following: a State of the United States; the District of Columbia; Puerto Rico ; the Virgin Islands; … American Samoa; Guam; Wake Island; Eniwetok Atoll; Kwajalein Atoll; and Johnston Island.

Oppressive child labor ” means a condition of employment under which (1) any employee under the age of sixteen years is employed by an employer (other than a parent or a person standing in place of a parent employing his own child or a child in his custody under the age of sixteen years in an occupation other than manufacturing or mining

figures.finding: Where the federal Act reaches (Wake and Johnston Islands), its child-labour section doesn't apply to a child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures, theatre, radio or television, so a child performer there has no federal age limit or permit; the exemption names actors and performers only, not a young writer or director, who stays under the general rule. Elsewhere in the islands no rule applies.
figures.applies: Federal law where it reaches; no state law applies in the islands.
